# NPM Improved v1.6.0 — NPMX write-through configuration management

### Edit from either node

NPMX secondaries can accept normal JSON configuration CRUD requests (proxy hosts,
redirects, 404 hosts, streams, access lists, certificates metadata, settings and
users) while the primary remains the authoritative database. You no longer have
to know which node your load balancer or shared public hostname served to
make ordinary edits.

- The secondary validates the locally authenticated user and obtains a
  fingerprint of its current record.
- It negotiates NPMX version/capabilities with its configured primary, and
  forwards the operation using the existing HMAC-signed, replay-protected
  NPMX peer connection.
- The primary validates the initiating account again, runs the same original
  API authorization, input validation, apply/rollback and Nginx tests, and
  **allocates all new record IDs** on the primary.
- A primary-side mutation lock serializes incoming and local writes.
- If the primary record differs from the last synchronized secondary copy,
  the operation returns HTTP **409 Conflict**. The newer primary change is
  retained; the stale secondary write is not silently substituted.
- On a successful write, the secondary schedules a prompt configuration pull.
  Normal NPMX polling continues at the configured 30-second default.

**Conflict ordering:** DB row IDs from different nodes are not timestamps.
The primary establishes a deterministic order for committed writes.
Conflicting edits based on stale snapshots are rejected rather than guessed
from unsynchronized wall clocks. The user may refresh to see the newer state
and then submit a new change.

### Availability and safety

- Both nodes must be on v1.6.0 for write forwarding. The existing mixed-version
  guard prevents unsafe replication during rolling upgrades.
- A secondary **fails closed** when the primary is unreachable; it cannot
  safely allocate a conflicting record ID or apply an uncommitted change.
- The configured NPMX Primary URL must resolve to the **actual primary node**,
  not a shared load-balanced host that may route back to another secondary.
  The public browser URL can still be shared across your nodes.
- Signed JSON configuration operations are supported. Multipart certificate
  uploads, disaster-recovery restores and config-history restores must be
  performed on the primary pending purpose-built transactional asset transfer.
- On first pairing or upgrade to v1.6.0, secondary browser sessions issued
  before the synchronized user database was established are rejected for
  writes. Sign out and back in once using an account from the primary.
  Routine later snapshots do **not** force repeated sign-ins.
- Authentication/permissions remain evaluated on the primary. Analytics and
  blocking observations stay local to the responding node.
- No Docker helper containers or new network-side services.

This release leaves all existing Host Analytics, node-local Analytics Center,
Nginx traffic serving and native updater logic intact.
